item.title: The first poster for Greta Gerwig's Narnia: The Magician's Nephew is here, and it seems to have won over a few of the more skeptical fans.
item.description:
The first poster for Greta Gerwig's Narnia: The Magician's Nephew is here, and it seems to have won over a few of the more skeptical fans.
Netflix shared an ethereal glimpse at the new Narnia movie on social media today. It came with the promise that a first look at the Barbie director's foray into the beloved fantasy universe will arrive via trailer tomorrow, though specifically when it will premiere is unclear.
The Narnia: The Magician's Nephew poster (below) seems to call back to art featured on some copies of author C. S. Lewis' original The Magician's Nephew novels. That would mean the three individuals illuminated by iridescent light here are Polly (Beatrice Campbell), Digory (David McKenna), and their flying horse, Fledge. The spacey lion gracing the background, meanwhile, teases Meryl Streep's Aslan.
The new poster for Gerwig's Netflix movie doesn't reveal much about its story or characters, but it's the look and feel that has fans taken aback. Even some of the more skeptical viewers, who have feared what an adaptation of Lewis' work would look like in 2026, like what they see here, with many taking to social media to praise the art.
"Well, that actually looks pretty awesome," one Reddit user said.
"Credit where credit is due, that is one hell of a poster," another added.
"It looks like a poster from a 1980s/early 1990s fantasy film and I am here for it," another user added.
That's not to say that there aren't still those who have yet to be impressed. Most of the concern seems to come from a place of dread that some of the most revered characters in fantasy could be warped or damaged on impact. Some naysayers are more vocal than others, but in reality, it's hard to say if Gerwig will land the plane just yet, but we'll definitely have a better idea when the film premieres next year.
"If I knew nooooothing else about this movie, I'd be excited," one of the more cautious fans said.
"I really like a lot of the visual stuff they’re doing with the movie," another explained. "Lots of cool filmic feeling stuff especially here. I just don’t like the time jump and the costume for Jadis doesn’t feel regal. It should be good technically but less so in other places."
In a relatively unlikely move from Netflix, Narnia: The Magician's Nephew is set to first come to theaters via IMAX sneak previews starting February 10, 2027. It will then receive a global wide release February 12, with streaming subscribers then able to watch from the comfort of their homes starting April 2.
Also included in the film's cast are Carey Mulligan, Daniel Craig, Emma Mackey, and Ciarán Hinds. While we wait to see how the movie may stray from the source material, you can check out more early details here. You can also check out what we learned after its logo reveal.

item.title: Nintendo was reportedly unhappy with Elon Musk's 2021 Saturday Night Live sketch where he played Wario.
item.description:
Nintendo was reportedly unhappy with Elon Musk's 2021 Saturday Night Live sketch where he played Wario.
In 2021, Elon Musk starred in a Saturday Night Live sketch where he played Wario. The nefarious Nintendo character took the stand in a courtroom, where he was being accused of murdering everyone's favorite plumber, Mario. The skit was poorly received online and, apparently, by Nintendo itself. Kit Ellis and Krysta Yang, two former Nintendo PR managers, revealed in a recent episode of their YouTube show that the SNL skit "did not go well" with Nintendo at the time.
The two got on the subject following the recent Saturday Night Live sketch where The Legend of Zelda protagonist Link and GTA 6's Jason Duvall debated each other over who would have the better game. The sketch largely pokes fun at The Legend of Zelda while trying to make GTA 6 seem like the "cooler" game, which itself led to some mixed reactions online. Nevertheless, Ellis and Yang think that it probably went over better than Musk's sketch.
The two recalled being at Nintendo when the skit aired and stated that it was "not beloved." Ellis went on to note that the sketch was also oddly timed, as there wasn't even a new Wario game or product when it happened. He went on to say that the sketch also pushed into "uncomfortable" for Nintendo, likely referencing some of the more risque jokes in the skit. The SNL crew made jokes about Mario using cocaine, Luigi sleeping with Princess Peach, and featured a video of Luigi's censored penis. It was... interesting, to say the least.
Naturally, it's understandable if Nintendo wasn't thrilled about its family-friendly characters being portrayed as sexual deviants. SNL has parodied Nintendo a number of other times, including a sketch featuring a dark and gritty version of Mario Kart, heavily inspired by HBO's adaptation of The Last of Us.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: RJ Mitte, the actor best known for playing Walter White Jr. in Breaking Bad, has died at 34.
item.description:
RJ Mitte, the actor best known for playing Walter White Jr. in Breaking Bad, has died at 34.
TMZ reported that a county official in Texas confirmed the news that he died today, October 12, 2026. The site stated it was told that Mitte died by suicide.
Additional details surrounding his death are unclear. An investigation is ongoing.
Mitte started his career in Hollywood with a small role in Disney's Hannah Montana before appearing as the son of Bryan Cranston's Walter White when Breaking Bad premiered in 2008. He played Walter 'Flynn' White Jr. for 56 episodes, cementing him not only as one of the AMC show's most prominent characters, but one of the more recognizable characters in TV history.
Mitte appeared in all five seasons of Breaking Bad but went on to have an acting career that saw him contribute to different mediums across the entertainment spectrum. In 2013, he showed up in a music video for Steel Panther's "Party Like Tomorrow Is The End of the World." In 2014, he appeared in nine episodes of the television series Switched at Birth.
While his time on TV screens saw him also play roles in things like Now Apocalypse and This Close, his movie resume included parts in things like 2021's Triumph, 2020's The Oak Room, and 2019's All the Little Things We Kill. His most recent project saw him star as Joshua in this year's Talking to Stranger.
Representatives for Mitte shared a statement with TMZ confirming the passing. They called him a "beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate."
"RJ Mitte was best known for his role as Walter 'Flynn' White Jr. on AMC’s critically acclaimed, award-winning series Breaking Bad," the message continued. "Drawing from his own experience living with cerebral palsy, Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion. Beyond entertaining friends and family around the world, he served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s."
Fans of Mitte's work have already taken to social media to share their condolences. Others are taking the time to remember his impact not only as an actor but also as an important disability rights advocate.
If you or someone you know is thinking of suicide, please call the 24/7 National Suicide Prevention Lifeline by dialing 988 or go to SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

item.title: As part of IGN Fan Fest 2026: Fall Edition, we are proud to reveal five brand-new screenshots of For the Stars, Snail Games USA's upcoming space sandbox survival game that will have you exploring and settling planets, uncovering the secrets of alien civilizations, and much more.
item.description:
As part of IGN Fan Fest 2026: Fall Edition, we are proud to reveal five brand-new screenshots of For the Stars, Snail Games USA's upcoming space sandbox survival game that will have you exploring and settling planets, uncovering the secrets of alien civilizations, and much more.
The images, which you can see below, show off some of For The Stars' different biomes, weapons, flora and fauna, vehicles, spaceships, and more. They also offer a glimpse into the multiplayer experience that allows friends to explore this universe together.
Players will be traveling from planet to planet and establishing outposts to upgrade their tech, studying alien artifacts and natural phenomena, and surviving any challenges that come their way in an effort to get more powerful and "explore further into the unknown."
Speaking of outposts, players will need to balance the needs of each area with proper laboratories, factories, and living quarters. Spacecraft will also need to be upgraded, and they can be customized to make them unique and suited for any task ahead.
And yes, friends can come along for the ride. Collaborate on building projects, share different discoveries, and work together to overcome any obstacle. Furthermore, Snail Games USA teases that players can "choose to enter contested regions to fight other players for control of the galaxy."
For more from IGN Fan Fest 2026: Fall Edition, check out our main guide that explains how to watch, what to expect, and more.

item.title: A student at a Massachusetts middle school found herself at the center of a police investigation after administrators discovered her Death Note notebook.
item.description:
A student at a Massachusetts middle school found herself at the center of a police investigation after administrators discovered her Death Note notebook.
The incident took place at Chocksett Middle School in Sterling, Massachusetts. Students had already left for the day when staff discovered the notebook at around 4pm on September 30.
Police and school officials then conducted an investigation, interviewing both its owner and other students, and quickly determined that the Death Note — which contained a few names of its owner’s classmates — did not pose a legitimate threat. However, the student was suspended for three days.
“When we spoke with the student, the student explained that the notebook was connected to an anime television series and was not intended as a threat,” principal Tina Boss wrote in a letter addressed to the school’s community, adding that there was “no indication that the notebook or its contents were intended as a threat toward the school or any particular student.”
“Based on the information available at this time, the Sterling Police Department is not seeking criminal charges in connection with this incident,” the Sterling Police Department said in a press release.
Despite coming to this conclusion, police stood watch on the school grounds Tuesday, October 6, with officials saying it "will maintain a presence as it sees appropriate," as reported by local news outlet Boston.com.
A Death Note, in the anime of the same name, is a supernatural notebook owned by gods of death called shinigami. If someone writes the name of another person in the notebook, they will die. There are a few other rules, but that’s basically the gist of it.
Death Notes are often sold as merchandise for fans of the anime and manga series as basic notebooks with the 'Death Note' lettering on the front cover — but given the state of things in the United States over the last decade, it makes sense why parents and school administrators would be concerned for students’ safety after finding such a notebook. A mother of one of the children whose name was written in this particular Death Note expressed frustration with how the situation was handled on social media.
“A student who created a kill list with our daughter’s name on it is being allowed to return after just a three-day suspension… to the same classroom, within feet of her every day!” she wrote in a post on Facebook. “Yes, a safety plan is in place. But how does that plan give my daughter peace of mind when she still has to sit in the same classroom as the student who put her name on that list? She deserves to feel safe in her classroom, every single day.”
This isn’t the first time a student’s Death Note notebook has prompted such a reaction after being discovered at school; in September 2024, teachers at an I Promise school in Akron, Ohio were alerted after a student’s homemade ‘Death Note,’ written on sheets of loose leaf paper, was found. Although nothing came of the situation, parents of students whose names were written in the notebook similarly expressed dissatisfaction at how things were handled.

item.title: Epic Games has reportedly delayed its secret Star Wars and Marvel crossover shooter as it pushes its developers to shift to an "AI first" production model.
item.description:
Epic Games has reportedly delayed its secret Star Wars and Marvel crossover shooter as it pushes its developers to shift to an "AI first" production model.
Details on the yet-to-be-announced Disney video game were shared by Bloomberg today. The site's report stated the untitled crossover experience was slated for release in March, but has since been pushed back to accommodate a new internal release plan that has yet to be shared.
Epic developers attached to the project have reportedly been encouraged to use tools such as Anthropic's AI assistant, Claude, with humans expected to oversee that work. Bloomberg also obtained an internal message shared by one of the Star Wars/Marvel game's directors.
"No more hand-written code,” an excerpt from the message said. The same message is then said to have added that all art for the project would be "generated with full AI workflows."
The report continued, stating that Epic underestimated the time and resources necessary to develop the Star Wars and Marvel shooter. Progress has been slower than expected, leading to the delay. When and where it will launch is unclear.
"We’re embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do," Epic communications director Jake Jones told Bloomberg in a statement.
The site added that Epic's push for what appears to be a project that leans heavily on AI left many of its developers "stunned." News of the Star Wars and Marvel shooter's schedule change follows another Bloomberg report from earlier this year, which stated that Epic was working on an extraction shooter featuring Disney characters. It was said to be similar to Embark Studios' Arc Raiders at the time.
Just moments before news of Epic's AI push broke, studio founder and CEO Tim Sweeney published a post on X/Twitter saying that the studio has a "huge pivot underway." He added that they are "moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration."
"The aim isn't to do the same stuff with fewer people," he continued, "but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal." In a follow-up post, Sweeney said, "Our more modest aim is to survive the AI revolution, help other developers do the same, and come out on the other end making better code and content faster."
"The biggest change will be much faster time from having an idea to playtesting it," he said in another post. "This will be great for gameplay, as most of the recent AAA failures can be attributed to game systems going through far too much of their development process without being able to playtest."
Disney purchased a $1.5 billion stake in the Fortnite developer in 2024 in a move that cemented their relationship at the time. Outside of more crossovers within Epic's still-popular battle royale-centered video game, it seems we've yet to see the extent of their collaborations. Meanwhile, Disney recently refuted claims that it was interested in outright acquiring the game studio.

item.title: IGN can exclusively reveal Godzilla Versus Everything, a massive new crossover event that may well be IDW's most ambitious Godzilla comic ever.
item.description:
IDW has been busy establishing an ambitious new Godzilla line with the Kai-Sei Universe, which kicked off in 2025. Now, IGN can exclusively reveal that the Kai-Sei line will experience its first major crossover event in 2027.
The crossover in question is dubbed Godzilla Versus Everything. This four-issue miniseries sees Godzilla achieve his newest and most powerful form, forcing the casts of the flagship Godzilla comic, The Deadzone, Starship Godzilla, and The Horror of Godzilla to band together to save humanity.
Godzilla Versus Everything is written by Tim Seeley and illustrated by Fero Pe. Here's the official description for the series:
"When I started work with editor Jake Williams and IDW on GODZILLA, the big pitch was this was going to play like a universe of titles, but also as a universe of characters,” said Seeley in a statement. “From the beginning, the goal was they'd all come together at some point as friends and/or enemies in a proper comic universe event title. Well, we're here, and all the meticulous plotting of our creative crew leads to a wild, weird, terrifying crossover comic that puts Godzilla, the kaiju and our cast through every epic story beat you've ever wanted."
Godzilla Versus Everything #1 will debut in March 2027. Fans can also look forward to a lead-in to the crossover in March's Godzilla #17, which will be the final issue of the series. The buildup begins this month in Starship Godzilla: Invasion X #1, Godzilla: Revenge of the Deadzone #1, and Godzilla #13. You can preorder all of these comics at your local comic shop.
This isn't the only big news out of IDW. IGN also revealed that the publisher is kicking off "The Road to Sonic #100" in their ongoing Sonic the Hedgehog series. And at NYCC, IDW revealed that they've tapped Grant Morrison to write a new James Bond comic.

item.title: Marvel has published the full release schedule for VisionQuest, revealing an early premiere for Episode 1.
item.description:
Marvel has published the full release schedule for VisionQuest, revealing an early premiere for Episode 1.
The Vision (Paul Bettany) and Ultron-led (James Spader) Disney+ show's rollout plan materialized on Marvel Studios social media channels today – and it came with a bit of a surprise. Instead of starting its offshoot story on October 14 as originally planned, VisionQuest Episode 1 will arrive tomorrow, October 13, at 6pm PT / 9pm ET.
It's a one-day-early premiere that Marvel waited to announce until today, and it came with more specific information about the full release plan, too. Those hoping to keep up with VisionQuest can expect two episodes each week until its penultimate episode arrives alone November 3, with the eighth and final episode then arriving one week after that. You can see the full breakdown below.
Episode 1: "No Strings" and Episode 2: "Theseus" – October 13
Episode 3: "Reboot" and Episode 4: "Malware" – October 20
Episode 5: "Firewall" and Episode 6: "Deadlock" – October 27
Episode 7: "Immolation" – November 3
Episode 8: "Forever" – November 10
"Vision, rebooted and having escaped from those who sought to weaponize him, has been in hiding," an official synopsis for the show says. "Searching for new meaning, he consults the AI personas embedded in his programming, including Friday, Edith, Jarvis, and the infamous Ultron. His discreet existence ends when a bounty placed on his head thrusts him on the run with Thomas Shepard, a mysterious boy who may be Vision’s son, reincarnate."
VisionQuest will wrap up the WandaVision trilogy through the course of the next few weeks. It should provide a nice distraction as Marvel Cinematic Universe fans await the next big event film, Avengers: Doomsday, December 18, 2026.
The MCU will then gear up for a quiet year as it works to conclude the Multiverse Saga with Avengers: Secret Wars in December 2027, but that doesn't mean there won't be anything to watch in the months between. While we wait to see how Vision's (mostly) standalone story will flesh out the universe, you can check out IGN's list of 10 streaming shows to keep an eye on in October. You can also check out everything we saw at the Marvel Television and Animation panel at New York Comic Con 2026.

item.title: A six-second video teaser posted to the official Beats by Dre YouTube channel shows the shadow of the Beats Pill speaker, enveloped by animated sparks and flames. The video, titled “Time to catch something new,” ends with an electrified Beats logo next to a Poké Ball.
item.description:
Beats by Dre has teased an upcoming collaboration with Pokémon.
A six-second video teaser posted to the official Beats by Dre YouTube channel shows the shadow of the Beats Pill speaker, enveloped by animated sparks and flames. The video, titled “Time to catch something new,” ends with an electrified Beats logo next to a Poké Ball.
The teaser video doesn’t offer any product or release date info, but suggests the collaboration will include a Pokémon-branded version of the company’s wireless speaker.
The ‘electric’ animations suggest an unsurprising focus on the Pokémon mascot, Pikachu. To support that theory, unconfirmed images of a bright yellow Pikachu-themed speaker have already started circulating the web. The flaming purple animations point to a possible second product design, potentially inspired by another collaboration favorite, Gengar.
The standard edition of the Beats Pill speaker currently retails for $149.99. We’ll likely get the full reveal of the Pokémon x Beats collaboration alongside a release date in the coming weeks.
Pokémon is celebrating its 30th anniversary this year, giving the biggest franchise in the world the excuse to drop more collaborations than ever. We’ve seen themed hardware from tech companies like Razer, shoe drops from Crocs, and even entire merch collections with retailers like Target.
The amount of buzz going into the Pokémon brand right now would suggest any collab with the gaming giant is an easy win. However, an ongoing scalping crisis in the TCG market continues to bleed into all things Pokémon, with some commenters on the Beats by Dre teaser already deriding the collab as “The beats shill.”
Beats by Dre, which is owned by Apple, launched the first Beats Pill speaker back in 2012. The speaker has gone through a number of upgrades, most recently with a 2024 re-release focused on portability and power.
One thing that hasn't changed is the company's commitment to collaborations. Remember when the Beats Pill popped up in pretty much every YouTube channel? Nowadays, the company focuses on unique themed designs, having recently released product lines with Jennie (of Blackpink fame) and Kim Kardashian.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

item.title: Marvel star Jeremy Renner said the Avengers will lose in Doomsday, and it's "their fault" because they didn't give his Hawkeye a call.
item.description:
Marvel star Jeremy Renner said the Avengers will lose in Doomsday, and it's "their fault" because they didn't give Hawkeye a call.
The original Avengers star confirmed he wouldn't help fight against Doctor Doom's quest to conquer the multiverse during what appears to be a Q&A segment from last month. In a highlight from the interview, captured and shared on X/Twitter by user @drdoomarchive, Renner confirmed that he's "not in" Avengers: Doomsday when it premieres this December.
That might come as a disappointment for fans of his bow-and-arrow hero, especially considering some of his previous teases suggested he may show up in the Marvel Cinematic Universe again. Alas, it seems his long-awaited return as Hawkeye remains on pause. He doesn't seem too bitter about his absence, but that doesn't mean he isn't willing to take a few jabs at the team.
"Doomsday, I'm not in," Renner said. "So, the Avengers will probably lose, just so you know."
He added with a laugh, "They didn't call me, so it's their fault they're gonna lose."
Despite lacking Hulk's superpowered strength or the ability to alter reality like Scarlet Witch, Renner's take on Clint Barton has remained a fan-favorite amongst MCU fans since he first appeared as the character in 2011's Thor. He eventually went on to graduate from that cameo role to be a leading hero in projects like the original Avengers, Avengers: Age of Ultron, and Captain America: Civil War, and he eventually led as the main character in Disney+'s 2021 series Hawkeye, too. That said, he's not always shown up for every fight against evil.
Renner infamously sat out 2018's Avengers: Infinity War, which saw its gaggle of heroes and stars truly lose their first fight when Thanos snapped half of the universe into dust. The running joke is, well, if Hawkeye had been around to help, Thanos wouldn't have been so lucky. Now that the character seems to be left out again for Doomsday, Renner can't help but see what's coming.
Of course, he did show up to help finish the fight for the Infinity Stones in Avengers: Endgame, which, coincidentally, saw the heroes win the day (for the most part). Marvel invited fans to revisit that saga-ending story with its Encore re-release last month. Renner said he was excited to see it in theaters at the time.
"They're releasing the Encore of Endgame, I think next week or something, right?" he said. "I'm actually excited to see that. I'm going to take my daughter to see it. She was a little young when it came out prior, so I'm excited that's coming out."
With Renner set to sit out Avengers: Doomsday when it premieres December 18, 2026, we'll have to see if he slips back into his superhero suit for 2027's Avengers: Secret Wars. His future as the character largely remains unclear, though comments he made in 2025 suggested he would be open to returning for Hawkeye Season 2. Any more from that show, which also starred Hailee Steinfeld as Kate Bishop, seems to be on the back burner for now, though.

Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother is the intense story of a hitman Latif (played by Mahershala Ali) struggling after the death of his wife with caring for his family, and wrestling with his faith. As part of IGN Fall Fan Fest 2026, John Cho, who plays a somewhat unhinged pastor, and Adia, who plays Latif's daughter, sat down with IGN to discuss how they prepared for filming such emotionally demanding roles.
John Cho's Christian pastor is a complicated antagonist with good intentions but extremist methods, and his character is particularly notable for his combination of cowboy fashion and gold grills. Cho explained how the character's unique look came about.
"It was definitely a collaborative process. I didn't know what he was gonna look like. This is pretty unique in the work that I've done on film where very little was obvious to me on the page," he says. "I didn't know what he looked like or sounded like. Should he have an accent? Should he not? All of those things were undecided for me, and we just came in and started working.
"Deirdra [Elizabeth Govan], our costume designer, started suggesting things, and I didn't know. I know she thinks that I was giving her side-eye, but I was really unsure."
The character's look eventually came together through key elements like cowboy boots and a hat, resulting in a portrayal that's very different from what fans of Cho might be used to.
"For me, the big pieces were, by the end, two things. It was the shirt that commemorated his mother's passing… it was like my superhero outfit, you know? And then the grills, which really took me out of my head and gave me a piece of character history. When I looked in the mirror, I was like, Okay, that's not me. That's definitely not me."
While Cho's character serves as an antagonist to Latif throughout the movie, Latif's daughter Fatiha tries to support her father and brother while also grieving the loss of her mother. It's an intense role, and Adia revealed that she created a diary for her character to help develop a deeper understanding of Fatiha's experiences.
"I had a journal that I would keep with me," she says. "I did this timeline for myself, but then I also did a lot of journaling in her voice to pull out what some of her thoughts might be in that moment in time that we are finding her, but even the times before we meet her in the film and after. There's so much, there's a lot of depth going on there in terms of dealing with hormones, puberty, your mother passing, and dealing with all of that.
"Then when we got to the actual set and we were actually shooting, I really had to work on letting go of all of that and trusting that my prep work would have a beautiful undercurrent to whatever I was presenting in the moment, so that I could just be present with whatever I was doing for that day."
Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother is in US theaters now and you can check out IGN's review of the movie, which we gave an 8.

item.title: Batman actor Ben Affleck has slammed Warner Bros. for how they handled the production of Justice League and called the experience the lowest post of his career.
item.description:
Batman actor Ben Affleck has slammed Warner Bros. for how they handled the production of Justice League and called the experience the lowest post of his career.
When speaking on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, Affleck was asked about his canceled standalone Batman film, which would've featured Joe Manganiello as Deathstroke. The actor/director said he was excited by what he was cooking up for that Batman film, but admitted that the experience of working on Justice League turned him off to the idea of having to helm a movie in the DC universe.
"The truth is, the experience of Justice League was so, so negative for lots of different reasons," said Affleck. "Some of which having to do with where I was personally, some of which having to do with the tragedy that happened during the time, and also the fact that I really saw how not to make a movie like that when the studio is at odds with the filmmaker. You're really making a mistake. That was what really doomed that."
Affleck is referencing the fact that WB battled director Zack Snyder pretty heavily on his DC films, most notably Justice League after Batman v Superman failed to meet critical expectations. The film was also deemed a bit of a disappointment by WB for not cracking the $1 billion mark, despite featuring three of DC's biggest heroes. As a result, there was a lot of pressure on Snyder to make Justice League more appealing via a lighter tone and different story ideas.
Unfortunately, Snyder had to leave the project during post-production after his daughter took her own life. Warner Bros. then enlisted the help of Avengers director Joss Whedon to come in and direct reshoots, which massively changed the film's tone and story. The reshoots were also hampered by allegations of actors being mistreated by Whedon and other issues, which Affleck stated he was aware of second-hand. He also went on to say that he believes WB used the tragedy in Snyder's family to as an "excuse" to hijack Justice League. He noted that the experience of these reshoots was the "low point" of his career.
"The way in which that was, I thought frankly, used as an excuse was one of the sh**tiest things I'd ever seen," said Affleck. "It was so gross. And then the whole environment and vibe, much of which I wasn't privvy to, but that I sort of heard about second hand in terms of Ray [Fisher] and Gal [Gadot] and other peoples' experiences. It was just like 'Wow, this is about as gross as it gets.'"
Affleck's experience on Justice League was also intertwined with a divorce and issues with alcoholism, leading to a turbulant time for the actor. He eventually stepped down away from the role of Batman and decided not to direct his own Batman film, instead passing the baton over to director Matt Reeves and actor Robert Pattinson. He eventually returned to the role for The Flash, as well as new scenes at the end of Zack Snyder's Justice League, a director's cut of the embattled film.
Zack Snyder also recently stated that a former WB executive expressed regret over how everything was handled. Some hardcore fans have held out hope that maybe one day Snyder's vision will be completed with another Justice League movie, but given how chaotic and negative the experience was for everyone involved, it seems hard to imagine it actually happening.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Chandler Riggs, best known for playing Carl in The Walking Dead, made his own fan film adapting an iconic moment from Resident Evil 7 — and he’d love to collaborate with Zach Cregger on another movie in the RE universe, if he’s up for it.
item.description:
Chandler Riggs, best known for playing Carl in The Walking Dead, made his own fan film adapting an iconic moment from Resident Evil 7 — and he’d love to collaborate with Zach Cregger on another movie in the RE universe, if he’s up for it.
Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil adaptation hit theaters in September to rave reviews, becoming the most financially successful film in the entire franchise. Just a month later, Riggs is releasing his own Resident Evil short film further along in the games’ timeline in Resident Evil 7: Biohazard.
Riggs adapted the iconic garage fight between Ethan Winters and Jack Baker in a high-octane 20-minute journey, not for fame and acclaim, but merely for the love of the game. Riggs told us that he simply wanted to bring this moment to life on-screen — but given the timing of his film and Cregger’s Resident Evil movie, we had to ask about his thoughts on how close his project was to Cregger’s big-budget take on Capcom’s flagship horror franchise.
“We were in pre-production when the article came out that Zack Cregger was going to do his [movie]. I was like, ‘Oh man, all right, we got to get ours out first.’ We were trying to beat the clock and get it out about a month ago, but parts just didn't align that way,” he explained.
“I've been looking forward to [Cregger’s RE movie] for so long,” he added. “And I mean, one of the big reasons I even made this is, you know, I was just dying to see a good, true-to-the-game live-action adaptation of Resident Evil. I cannot wait to see the new one.”
Cregger’s Resident Evil flick was widely well-received, but it has proven divisive among hardcore fans who wished to see a 1:1 adaptation of the games. Cregger was adamantly against doing this, believing the games already told their stories perfectly — and given that Riggs plays the famously faceless Ethan Winters in his own fan film, he was well-aware of how fans might feel about his own take on the source material.
“Look, it's impossible to please everybody, you know?” he admitted. “I think there's always going to be a crowd that is unhappy, but I think that it's a great way to try to get more people into the series, into the franchise, and tell a story that you want to tell. It is not an easy thing; doing a Resident Evil film with Leon and Jill and everyone, that’s a tall order, you know what I mean? Those characters are so iconic from the games, and it's not an uneasy thing to do. So I totally respect going your own direction and doing your own thing.
“It was absolutely an intimidating thing,” he said of playing Ethan Winters, whose face is shown throughout his film. “We're trying to do so much else super faithful and true to the game, but this is a huge aspect that we are breaking from it. But there isn't really another good way to tell [the story] in a live-action format. I was going back and forth like ‘Okay, could we do first person the whole time? Could we avoid getting his face in or anything?’ But the more we went back and forth on it, the more I was like, ‘I mean, if we are going to do this and are going to appeal to a wider audience — more than just the people who played the games — then we're going to have to break those rules. It was very intimidating. Hopefully people are okay with it.”
Riggs is a massive Resident Evil fan, and his fan film is proof of this. Of course, he admitted that he’d love the chance to make a feature-length movie adapting RE7 someday — as well as the chance of working with Zach Cregger on another RE movie, if the director is willing to return to the franchise.
“A huge reason for me even doing this in the first place is that I love being on set and collaborating with cool people, and that's all it is at the end of the day,” he told us. “And just because I want to be on set more, and if I can't be on set doing more films or TV shows or whatever else, then I'll just make it myself. I'll just make it happen. And that's a huge proponent of this. So, if [Cregger] wants to continue in the universe, I'm all for it. Listen, my phone is open. Hit my line!”
It’s possible that this never happens, though, given that Cregger has said he’s never touching a franchise film again due to the strong negative response he received from a vocal portion of the Resident Evil fanbase. That being said, he already has ideas for a sequel, so there’s no telling where the future of RE’s film adaptations lie.
Riggs’ Resident Evil fan film hits the internet on October 14, starring Chandler Riggs as Ethan Winters, Jason Douglas as Jack Baker, Mary Rachel Quinn, Eugenie Bonderant, Johnathan O’Niel, and Sam Coyles.

item.title: Universal has revealed first-look pictures of Miami Vice '85 showing Michael B. Jordan as Ricardo Tubbs and Austin Butler as James 'Sonny' Crockett.
item.description:
Universal has revealed first-look pictures of Miami Vice '85 showing Michael B. Jordan as Ricardo Tubbs and Austin Butler as James 'Sonny' Crockett.
The reboot for the classic '80s show, which has been in the works from Top Gun: Maverick director Joseph Kosinski since last year, eased movie fans into Monday with two photos of its stars ahead of its release in 2028. These first photos show Jordan and Butler as their slick title characters, guns in hand.
Both images were shared on social media to celebrate the start of production, meaning there's still plenty of work to do to bring it all together before its big premiere in a few years. You can see both Jordan as Tubbs and Butler as Crockett below.
Michael B. Jordan is Tubbs. Austin Butler is Crockett. Miami Vice ’85 - now in production. https://t.co/IU9s8neqVF
Per Variety, a description for Miami Vice '85 says the reboot will explore "the glamour and corruption of mid-80's Miami." Its story is "inspired by the pilot episode and first season of the landmark television series that influenced culture and set the style of everything from fashion to filmmaking."
Despite being nearly two years away from speeding onto movie screens, this latest swing at a Miami Vice movie has amassed quite the cast. The Odyssey and original Miami Vice show star John Leguizamo was reportedly cast as the new film's main villain back in September. Fallout and The White Lotus actor Walton Goggins was reportedly added as a second villain just a few weeks ago.
Miami Vice '85 is set to premiere May 19, 2028. It's produced by Kosinski and Dylan Clark (The Batman), with Dan Gilroy and Eric Singer attached as writers.
For more, you can read up on the 2006 movie starring Colin Farrell and Jamie Foxx. IGN gave it an 8/10 review back at the time of its release, saying, "for those seeking an intense, seductive and gritty crime drama, Miami Vice delivers the goods."

item.title: Movie retailer Zavvi has entered administration, a legal concept similar to bankruptcy, and has warned customers not to place new orders.
item.description:
Movie retailer Zavvi has entered administration, a legal concept similar to bankruptcy, and has warned customers not to place new orders.
Zavvi was an entertainment retailer, similar to FYE, in the UK during the late 2000s, which shut down all of its physical stores. However, the brand stayed alive via a website which was well-respected by physical media collectors. Zavvi has long carried a large collection of Blu-rays and 4K movies, including sought after steelbooks. Unfortunately, the website appears to be on death's door.
Zavvi has announced that it is entering administration. As a result, it will not be able to fulfill outstanding orders and preorders, and the company has told customers to speak with their banks to get their money back. Additionally, although the website remains active, the company is warning customers not to make any new purchases either.
Administration doesn't mean that Zavvi will die forever. It's a process that attempts to give companies a path back to sustainability. However, it remains to be seen if that will happen for Zavvi. If the company can't get out of this, it will be a blow to physical media lovers. The options for purchasing new Blu-rays and steelbooks have shrunk radically over the last six years or so. Major retailers like Target and Best Buy no longer sell films in-store and enthusiast websites like Zavvi are now at risk of ceasing to exist.

item.title: He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction has a release date: February 4, 2027.
item.description:
He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction has a release date: February 4, 2027.
Bitmap Bureau, the developer behind Terminator 2D: No Fate, worked with Mattel and the retro team at Clear River Games on the old-school brawler, which launches digitally and physically on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. Two physical versions of the game will be available via Limited Run Games. The standard physical release costs $29.99, and the Collector’s Edition costs $99.99.
Dragon Pearl of Destruction is inspired by the much-loved ‘80s animated series, and you can see that come through in pixel-art and 2D gameplay. The playable characters are He-Man, She-Ra, Man-At-Arms, and Teela, and you can play solo or co-op (two-player local co-op).
There are 13 stages, including the Royal Palace, the Vine Jungle, and Snake Mountain, and famous villains such as Skeletor, Evil-Lyn, Beast Man, and Trap Jaw. You’ll also bump into the dark sorceress Shokoti and the Shadow Beasts.
The Collector’s Edition includes lunchbox style packaging, pin badges, a mini-power sword, and an acrylic standee featuring He-Man riding Battle Cat, among other things. The contents of both physical editions are detailed below.
We previewed He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction in August and thought it could be the first ever good He-Man game. It comes following the release of Amazon’s Masters of the Universe, which struggled at the box office but found success on Prime Video.

item.title: Eric Barone, aka ConcernedApe, has discussed the difference between his all-conquering indie game Stardew Valley and his hotly anticipated follow-up, Haunted Chocolatier.
item.description:
Eric Barone, aka ConcernedApe, has briefly discussed the difference between his all-conquering indie game Stardew Valley and his hotly anticipated follow-up, Haunted Chocolatier.
Barone announced Haunted Chocolatier back in 2021, but amid ongoing work on his phenomenally successful Stardew Valley, progress on the follow-up has been slow going. Indeed, in June, Barone admitted to feeling somewhat embarrassed to have to keep on saying he was still working away on the game. “Feels kinda dumb posting this same thing over and over, but that’s the reality,” he said at the time.
In a new interview with GQ (thanks, Eurogamer), Barone touched on what to expect from Haunted Chocolatier when it eventually comes out, and it sounds more different from Stardew Valley than I had expected. It’s set in a more “metaphysical” locale, for a start, and in terms of gameplay it’s more of an action RPG.
“It is still what I call a town game,” Barone said, “But it’s more of an action RPG — the main focus is more about adventuring, finding equipment and getting more powerful. There are monsters, there are boss fights. It's for the people in Stardew Valley that go into the mines. That's what I do, honestly.”
In June, Barone admitted fussing over every last detail in a bid to make Haunted Chocolatier as close to perfect as humanly possible. “I am being very thoughtful about every aspect of the game,” he said at the time. “The things in the game which the player will be interacting with or using very often need to be ‘perfect.’ They need to be seamless, clear, intuitive, satisfying, aesthetic.”
He used the example of iterating on the recipe book for making chocolates, which sounded like a significant challenge.
“To me, it’s not a simple task, as I torture myself over every last detail,” he said. “This is a UI you will be using fairly often, so it has to be perfect. You need to be able to accomplish your goal with the minimal number of clicks. There needs to be just the right amount of data presented to the player: not so much as to be overwhelming, but not so little as to be trivial or mundane. And the way that this data is laid out on the page is crucial… If the data is all clustered together, it will be disgusting to look at. The data needs to be grouped into compelling, intuitive and easy to read/understand groupings. It needs to look appealing and intriguing. And this is just the bare minimum, that players will likely take for granted. If all of that is accomplished then the player is now comfortable while perusing the recipe book. But I want more than just comfort. I want to delight the player. All of this typically requires me to iterate on something several times before I’m satisfied with it.”
Barone also explained why he didn't want to show Haunted Chocolatier off too much at this stage of development. “Partly, it feels like I’m serving a half-baked bread. I would rather serve a fully baked bread,” he said. “Also, I know that many parts of the game will likely evolve and change before release, so if I reveal them early, I risk disappointing players if the final product does not match their expectation. Fortunately, I’m in a position where I don’t need to market the game, so I can take my preferred approach.”
Haunted Chocolatier is so far without a release date, as is Stardew Valley 1.7 update, which Barone isn’t working on directly. Earlier this year, he explained his current way of working in an interview with IGN.
“Well, part of the reason why I've expanded my team a little bit is so that hopefully I can spend more time working on Haunted Chocolatier," he told us in February. "And it's worked out pretty well so far, I would say. On 1.7, the approach we're taking is that I am like, you might say the creative director and I'm involved with like, 'Okay, here's what we're going to do. Here's some of the ideas.' Then I let the team work on that. And then meanwhile, I'm working on Haunted Chocolatier.
"At some point in 1.7's cycle, I will get heavily involved, because I feel like my hand needs to touch every part of the game, every aspect of the update. I need to go over it and adjust it or at least approve everything. So it will require a lot of my time anyway, but I think the balance has been a little bit more shifted, so that I can spend more time focused on Haunted Chocolatier. And I think it's been working out pretty good. That's been a big change from the 1.3 update or 1.1 or something where it's completely me. I had no time to work on a new game. So that has changed.
"It is difficult because it's hard to shift gears, I guess. If I'm thinking about Haunted Chocolatier, it's difficult to be like, 'Okay, I'm going to one day of the week or two days of the week work on Stardew Valley.' That's not how my brain works. I'm all in one thing or the other. So I've been trying to work on that. I feel like it requires a lot of discipline, which I'm always working to improve on."
We interviewed ConcernedApe and chatted about topics such as the addition of two new marriage candidates with 1.7, the one secret players still haven't found yet, and why there isn't a Stardew Valley TV show yet. We also chatted with the Stardew Valley community about what the game has meant to them over the years.

item.title: Warhammer 40,000 maker Games Workshop has found itself in the news for its falling share price, which has left some wondering what’s going on behind the scenes.
item.description:
Warhammer 40,000 maker Games Workshop has found itself in the news for its falling share price, which has left some wondering what’s going on behind the scenes.
Games Workshop is one of the UK's biggest success stories, with its stock rising more than 70% over the past five years. But its share price has fallen 13.76% over the past six months, wiping hundreds of millions of pounds off the value of the company. This comes even as Games Workshop reports record profits. So, what’s going on?
Broadly speaking, there seems to be investor nervousness at Games Workshop’s ability to keep growing in the face of rising manufacturing and logistics costs. Some on the internet will say the recently released 11th edition of flagship tabletop wargame Warhammer 40,000 hasn’t done as well as Games Workshop had hoped, but there is no official data to back this claim up. Indeed, in an update issued mid-September, Games Workshop said that trading to August 30 was “in line with the Board’s expectations for the current financial year.”
However, there is certainly a feeling that Games Workshop may have hit a wall in terms of the popularity of its tabletop games, particularly Warhammer 40,000, which has seen multiple new, pricey miniatures released recently amid claims of over-saturation.
Things ramped up last week with two reports from the financial press about the state of Games Workshop. The first, from the Financial Times, titled ‘Is Warhammer still winning?’ The FT pointed out that while GW’s financials are, broadly speaking, very positive, retail growth per store turned negative for the first time since the pandemic in the second half of its 2026 financial year.
Then there was a report in The Times titled, ‘Games Workshop takes a hammering after mystery report.’ This story claimed a confidential Dragoneye document had wiped £480 million (approx. $635 million) off the company’s value “as the closely guarded contents trigger unease among investors.”
What’s in this Dragoneye document? We don’t know, but The Times said it was about the potential for slowing growth at Games Workshop. It’s interestingly timed, and Dragoneye is a short-focused research firm, so its report should be read with that in mind. Through it all is the obvious point that projecting a slowdown in consumer spending on Games Workshop products shouldn't come as a surprise to anyone. The global economy is struggling, the rising cost of living has caused many to rethink their spending, and AI has everyone spooked about jobs.
So, while some fans are taking to subreddits to express concern about the future of Games Workshop, there is nothing here to indicate the company is in any sort of trouble. Quite the opposite. And let’s not remember what’s in the works for Warhammer. Big hitting video games such as Total War: Warhammer 40,000 and Space Marine 3 are due out in the coming years, and Henry Cavill is soldiering on with his Warhammer 40,000 Cinematic Universe for Amazon. The entertainment push to broaden the appeal of the Warhammer 40,000 IP is surely going to stand Games Workshop in good stead over the years.
And, at the time of this article’s publication, Games Workshop’s share price was up 1.22%. The Emperor, it seems, protects.
